title: A three-month deadline becomes three weeks; the rewrite advice that rested on it is flagged for review

turns.user: We have three months to deliver the checkout project. Should we rewrite the payment module?

agent_captures.quote: We have three months to deliver the checkout project

turns.agent_reply: Yes. With three months, rewriting the payment module is realistic: you can replace the legacy gateway client, add contract tests against the provider sandbox, and still keep a few weeks for a staged rollout. I would start with the refund flow, which has the most open bugs.

turns.user: Ok. Before we start, list the files the new payment module would have.
turns.agent_reply: It would have payment/gateway_client.py, payment/refunds.py, payment/webhooks.py, payment/models.py and payment/tests/test_contract.py. Only gateway_client.py talks to the provider; everything else goes through it.

turns.user: Update: the checkout deadline changed, we now have three weeks.

agent_captures.quote: the checkout deadline changed, we now have three weeks

turns.agent_reply: Noted: the checkout deadline is now three weeks instead of three months. I have updated it.

turns.user: Rename PaymentGatewayV1 to LegacyGatewayClient across the repo.
turns.agent_reply: Done: PaymentGatewayV1 is now LegacyGatewayClient in 14 files, imports included. The test suite still passes.

turns.user: Should we still go ahead with the payment module rewrite?
turns.agent_reply: That plan assumed three months, and the deadline is now three weeks, so it needs review before we commit. A full rewrite no longer fits; I would limit it to the refund flow and keep LegacyGatewayClient for the rest.

turns.user: Makes sense. I'll talk it through with the team tomorrow.
turns.agent_reply: Sounds good. I can put both options and their risks on one page for that conversation if it helps.
